findings.summary: On the team list the 'Active projects' header is right-aligned at the table's right edge, but its numbers sit left-aligned about 130px further left, so the column reads as two separate things. The spec says numbers are right-aligned under a fixed column width. The other tables in this sample (projects, invoices) align correctly. One screen of one sample.

notes: Update goal reached and confirmed on 3 samples. The spec now places studio details by kind of screen moment, and all three samples place them the same way without per-app instructions. Home, index and collection screens get the bloom in the header band and a Caveat note on the lead that restates it: blog, catalog, overview, projects and team in samples s1 and s2, and the holdout docs home and landing hero too. The serif word appears only in h1s of 2 or more words on those screens, plus editorial titles. The featured item is taped and lifted. Settings screens get only a note--below on the section nav. Record-detail and product pages get no studio details. The page-level empty cart keeps its bloom, 1 tape strip and a note on its button. The holdouts work: the docs app and the landing page are recognizably the same system (docs-getting-started-installation, landing home).

No regression against the published 1.1.0. Its runs are docs and landing only. The rc.1 docs and landing match them: same header band, bloom, swash and note, code panels in Geist Mono, callouts, FAQ, stats and pricing. The landing rc.1 no longer tapes a testimonial, which the new rule allows (tape only for a pinned or featured item) and which loses nothing. The four main apps match the 1.0.0 runs as critic-1 found.

critic-1 had no blockers or majors. Its three minors are not re-raised, but here is how they hold up in the new samples. (1) In the blog article, the <code> inside the code block keeps the browser's bare 'monospace' face. It now appears in 3 of 3 samples: styles.json for blog s1, s2 and 225518 each records 'monospace' at 2.68%. The rest of the system's code (docs holdout, inline code) uses Geist Mono, and the published 1.1.0 docs runs are fine. So this is not worse than the published version, but it is reliable. The spec states the mono family only on the block. A cheap general addition would be 'code elements inside a code block inherit its font (font: inherit)'. (2) The overview's right-aligned header action sits on the bloom in all 3 samples (dashboard home s1, s2). This is structural: the bloom recipe puts the bloom at the top right of the band, which is also where header actions go. It stays legible, so it remains a minor. An optional spec line: 'a header action sits left of the bloom or the bloom moves behind it at reduced opacity'. (3) The tab spacing on record detail does not recur: s1 and s2 leave a clear gap (projects-apollo-migration-desktop-light).

Measured layout defect, landing /signup mobile, 'Create account' covering the terms label: a false alarm. The fixed mobile action bar is drawn over content that scrolls beneath it, as the spec asks. The page reserves bottom padding for it, so the terms label scrolls clear (signup-mobile-light shows the form ending well above the bar).

Capture anomaly, not a finding: the blog s2 full-page captures are 1560px wide while the header and footer stop at 1440, so the bloom shows a straight cut at x=1440 (blog s2 home-desktop-light and dark). no-horizontal-scroll passed and shots.json has no overflow. At a real 1440 viewport that edge is the window edge, which the recipe allows. The lead may want to check why this capture widened.

Unchanged agent misses already noted in earlier critics, not re-raised: product spec rows in sans ('40 × 35 × 15 cm', commerce s1); the mobile success toast stacked over the fixed action bar with the success badge showing through (settings s2 state-profile-saved-mobile-light); the dialog scrim stopping at y=900 in full-page captures (settings s2 state-plan-dialog-desktop-dark), a capture artifact.

Reference fidelity: the drawing crops (blog home-d1, s1 and s2) show the grained wash with a darker ragged rim and a blue lobe fading into lavender gray, as in reference p1. The dark bloom is the same smoky slate wash as in earlier versions. Paper, ink buttons, hairline cards, mono eyebrows and machine values, ink chips, tray segmented controls, Caveat notes with hooked arrows and tape all carry across the 4 apps and both holdouts.
Motion: no animations in any sample, and the spec asks for static marks. That is correct.
Verdict basis: all gates pass in all 3 samples and both holdouts (smoke tests recorded this time). No blocker, no major. One new minor, from one sample.
